data.name: GetMeBro!
data.detailed_description:
Enter the battlefield and knock down your opponents in an unforgiving race for your life. Create the best strategy and ensure your victory by choosing from a variety of abilities. Customize your character, unlock new abilities, enter tournaments and much, much more. Play private games with your friends and spectate them on any device. Great fun for home/LAN parties.

100% skill based

The core of GetMeBro! is competitive balance. The right combination of abilities and your skill is the only way to be the best.

Build to be competitive

Ranked matchmaking ensures that every game is fair and balanced. Ingame tournaments offer a unique experience of eSport like events where you can not only win prizes but also watch other players and learn from them.

New challenging map every week

Battles are held on 3 distinguishable arenas that receive a new map every week. This makes players to adapt to new challenges and opens up a possibility for new strategies the become meta.

Stand out of the crowd with your unique look

Complete daily quest and win tournaments to get new outfits to customize your character. Rank-up all the way to the top of the ladder and unlock limited rewards.
A network connection is required for the first login and multiplayer matches, solo runs can be played without a connection.

reviews.review:
GetMeBro! is a really fast multiplayer game built around a simple idea that I actually find pretty fun. I am running through a dangerous obstacle course while another player is trying to do the same thing, and the goal is to survive long enough to create enough distance between us. It looks like a basic platforming game at first, but the real challenge comes from having to deal with the map, collect energy and decide when to use my abilities. The post apocalyptic setting is mostly there to give the game some personality, because the actual focus is on quick reactions and trying to outplay the person on the other side.

The movement is simple but takes some practice. I have to dodge blades, traps and other obstacles while keeping my character moving forward, and small mistakes can quickly turn into a loss. I like that the map is the same for both sides because it means I am not simply hoping for a better random layout. I can learn the routes, remember dangerous sections and work out where I need to be more careful. The maps also change regularly, which gives me a reason to adapt instead of relying on exactly the same route forever.

The ability system is probably the most interesting part for me. I collect energy during a run and can spend it on abilities that can make me faster, protect me or interfere with my opponent. That means I am constantly making a choice between saving energy for something useful later or spending it immediately to get an advantage. I like this because it gives the platforming a small strategic layer without making the controls complicated. I can play aggressively and try to force a mistake, or concentrate on surviving and let my opponent take the bigger risks.

There is also a proper ranked system with multiple ranks and tournaments, along with private matches where I can play without affecting my ranking. Character customisation gives me another little reason to keep playing, with outfits that are purely cosmetic rather than giving me an unfair gameplay advantage. I appreciate that because the competition stays focused on movement, reactions and how well I use my abilities. There are also achievements and daily quests, so there is some extra progression around the main matches rather than everything being completely reset after each race.

The biggest problem for me is that the game depends heavily on having a good multiplayer experience. The actual gameplay is enjoyable when everything is working properly, but there is not a huge amount of variety outside the core race. I can practise in training mode and play solo runs, but the main appeal is clearly the head to head competition. The game was also released on Steam as an early access title and the Steam page has not received a developer update for several years, which makes the whole project feel more like an older multiplayer game that has been left in its current state rather than something that is still growing.

I also think the simple structure limits how long I can stay interested at once. Learning a map and getting better at it is satisfying, but once I understand the basic movement and abilities, there are only so many things I can do differently. The weekly map changes help with this, but they do not completely solve the problem. I would have liked more modes or a larger selection of mechanics to make the experience feel more substantial outside the main one on one races.

Overall, I think GetMeBro! is a clever little multiplayer game that gets a lot out of its basic concept. I like the fast platforming, shared maps, energy based abilities, ranked system and cosmetic progression, and I think the game is at its best when I am learning a route and slowly getting better at reacting to its traps. The limited variety and dependence on multiplayer stop it from being something I would rate extremely highly, especially considering how old the current Steam version is. Still, the core idea is genuinely different and the matches are quick enough that I can jump in, play a few rounds and leave without feeling like I have wasted a huge amount of time.

Rating: 7.7/10
